notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Online play is on. GameCube and Wii games through Dolphin, and NES, SNES, Genesis and PlayStation games through RetroArch, can be played with another SCCM Retro console over the internet. Open a game's menu and choose Play Online. Host shows an 8-character code; the other player chooses Join, types the code, and the host presses Start when the roster shows them. Both consoles need the same game dump; the menu checks this before the match starts. The pause menu shows the players and the code during a session, and Leave ends it.

What to expect: GameCube and Wii sessions connect the two consoles directly, which works between two ordinary home connections but not from a mobile hotspot or an internet provider that uses carrier-grade NAT; those players can still play NES, SNES, Genesis and PlayStation, which go through SCCM Retro's own relay and work anywhere. PlayStation online uses a different emulator core than offline play, so it runs at the original resolution. If the host leaves, the other player returns to the menu within a second; if the host's console crashes, it takes about 20 seconds. Cheats are off during online play. N64, Dreamcast, PSP, DS, 3DS, PS2 and Wii U have no online play.

Find other players in the community Discord, in the channel for online play: post the game, the time, and your code.

New and lightly tested: online play was checked between two consoles on different networks by the developer; this is its first release to other people. Reports welcome.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
